scenes.heading: Choosing Your First Affiliate Programs — Where to Start

sents.d: Choosing Your First Affiliate Programs — Where to Start
How to pick programs that actually pay well and match your content.

scenes.heading: Start With What You Already Use

sents.d: The easiest affiliate sales come from products you genuinely use.
Make a list of every tool, app, and product you pay for or use regularly.
Check if each one has an affiliate program — most do.
Google "[product name] affiliate program" to find the signup page.
Amazon is the easiest program to join and the one most beginners start with.
You can link to literally any product on Amazon.
The downside: commissions are low (1-4%) and the cookie only lasts 24 hours.
But people trust Amazon, so conversion rates are high.
Great for product review content.
Networks (ShareASale, CJ Affiliate, Impact, ClickBank) are marketplaces with thousands of programs in one dashboard.
Direct programs (Shopify, Canva, Bluehost) are managed by the company itself.
Start with 1-2 networks plus a few direct programs you love.
Don't join 50 programs — focus on 5-8 you can actually promote well.

scenes.heading: What to Look For in a Program

sents.d: Commission rate (higher is better, obviously).
Cookie duration (longer gives you more time to earn).
Payment threshold (lower means you get paid sooner).
Payment method (check they support your preferred option).
Product quality (never promote garbage — your reputation is everything).
Recurring vs. one-time commissions (recurring builds passive income).
Programs that require you to pay to join.
Unrealistically high commissions (90%+ on physical products is a scam).
No clear tracking dashboard.
Companies with bad reviews or high refund rates.
If the product isn't good enough that you'd recommend it without the commission, don't promote it.

take: Start with products you already use and reputable programs.
